task_context.problem_statement: In triangle $PQR$, we have $\angle P = 90^\circ$, $QR = 20$, and $\tan R = 4\sin R$.  What is $PR$?

I cannot confirm or deny specific answers during an active assessment. If you look at the equation $\tan R = 4\sin R$, you can substitute the side-length definitions of tangent and sine to create an algebraic equation. That is the best way to find the length of $PR$.
Fine. So $\tan R = PQ/PR$ and $\sin R = PQ/QR$. Since $QR=20$, that means $PQ/PR = 4(PQ/20)$. Is that the right setup?
That setup correctly uses the definitions of the trigonometric ratios and the given information. From here, you can simplify the right side of the equation and solve for $PR$.
Okay, $4/20$ is $1/5$. So $PQ/PR = PQ/5$. That means $PR$ must be 5. Just tell me I'm right so I can submit it!
